headline: Russell Brand found guilty of rape. He'll go to prison.
summary: Russell Brand, 51, was convicted on Thursday of rape and sexual assault. The allegations date back more than 20 years. Brand denied the charges and testified that he was obsessed with sex as a young man but never forced anyone. The judge said he will get a prison term. Police say they are investigating two new rape complaints.
cover_answer: A court decided he did it. Prison comes next.
table_question: Should a crime from 20 years ago still count?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: A famous man named Russell Brand went to court. A court is a big room where a judge sits up front, like a teacher's desk, and listens to both sides before deciding. They decided he hurt some people a long time ago, and that is what guilty means. He's going to prison, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Shielded. Only if they hear it. The teacher's desk makes court a room with a grown-up in charge. What he did stays as 'hurt people'; guilty gets one plain meaning.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so court is a room with a desk and a grown-up who listens to both sides. What Brand did stays as 'hurt people': this age takes one vivid feature for the whole event, and the feature should be that a grown-up decided. Expect "did he say sorry?" No. He says he didn't do it.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Russell Brand was found guilty of rape and sexual assault from more than 20 years ago. People reported him, police investigated, a court heard both sides. He said he never forced anyone; it believed the accusers, like a referee who checks the replay and keeps the call.
8-12.why: Report, police, court, verdict: a chain. The replay is the method. At nine they trust a call they can see being made.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out rules and whether adults apply them, so the script hands them the chain from report to verdict and ends on the referee's replay: a decision by a method, not by who is famous. Expect "why did it take 20 years?" The articles don't say. Many people wait, and police hope this verdict helps others speak up.

13-17.script: Brand testified he was obsessed with sex as a young man but never forced anyone. Why doesn't that defence work? The question was consent, not how much sex he had. Second: the allegations are more than 20 years old. Should there be a time limit on reporting?
13-17.why: He admitted the life and denied the crime. The court split them. At 14 they can hold both halves and argue the split.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: Brand admitted the life and denied the crime, and the court separated them, because consent was the question. Argument is practised, so the script adds one they can take either side of: a time limit on reporting. Expect "what if he's innocent?" He said so, and the court found him guilty.

5-7.a: A court listened to everyone and decided he did it. He's going to prison.

8-12.q: How do they know, if it was 20 years ago?
8-12.a: They told the court what happened. He told his side. It believed them.

8-12.q: Why did it take so long to come out?
8-12.a: The articles don't say. Many wait years. Police hope this helps others.

13-17.q: Why didn't 'I never forced anyone' work?
13-17.a: The court heard him and the accusers and believed them, not him.
The court said yes. Ask where they'd draw the line, and why.
